extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, patent owners, and practitioners involved in PTAB inter partes review and Director review proceedings
extracted.subtask_short: director review of PTAB institution denial
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and considerations the USPTO Director applies when reviewing a Board decision denying institution of an inter partes review (IPR), including discretionary-denial factors (e.g., settled expectations), notice/opportunity to be heard, and the precedential force of informal guidance (FAQs/Boardside Chats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's broad discretion to institute or deny (35 U.S.C. § 314(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director retains broad authority to determine whether to institute an inter partes review; the decision to deny a petition is a matter committed to the Patent Office’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) and Cuozzo Speed Techs., LLC v. Lee, 579 U.S. 261, 273 (2016). This is a threshold principle: institution/denial decisions are discretionary and reviewed under abuse-of-discretion concepts. Arguments must show an abuse of that discretion to succeed on Director Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational Boardside Chat statements are not controlling authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements made during an informational Boardside Chat are not controlling authority or binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boardside Chat comments are merely informational; parties cannot treat them as binding limits on Director or Board discretion. Reliance on such informal statements cannot establish error in a discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQs / Interim guidance do not restrict the Director to party-raised arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAQs for Interim Processes (and later Interim Director Discretionary Process webpage) did not state or imply that 'unrequested issues will not be considered'; FAQs explained the Director would not consider discretionary denial without a request from a patent owner, and encouraged parties to address any fact or circumstance bearing on institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where FAQs invite party input, they do not bind the Director. The FAQs were later updated (see FAQ 10) to clarify the Director is not limited to the arguments the parties raise. Parties should not assume informal guidance prevents the Director from considering issues not expressly briefed by the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settled expectations of the parties is a discretionary consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Settled expectations of the parties" is an express factor in determining whether to deny institution or refer a petition to the Board (per the Process Memo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interim Processes for PTAB Workload Management (Process Memo) lists settled expectations as one factor and permits parties to brief discretionary considerations, including settled expectations. Parties should address whether and how the length of time a patent has been in force or other facts create settled expectations that weigh against institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties have notice and an opportunity to be heard on discretionary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Process Memo allowed parties to brief discretionary considerations (including settled expectations), and parties were encouraged to address any facts or circumstances bearing on institution, so failure to raise an argument does not necessarily mean there was inadequate notice or opportunity to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party claiming lack of notice must show the Process Memo/FAQs or Board procedure actually prevented meaningful briefing; mere failure to raise an argument (e.g., about its own settled expectations) does not prove the Office abused its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary denial is a holistic assessment of facts and circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether to exercise discretion to deny institution is based on a holistic assessment of all the facts and circumstances; many discretionary considerations may be relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner cannot succeed by cherry-picking a small number of decisions or considerations. The Director/Board evaluates the totality of circumstances (e.g., patent age, settled expectations, workload management, prior case treatment) rather than applying a single rigid rule across all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing disparate treatment requires distinguishing the facts of other cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguing the Office has 'declined to apply discretionary denial in similarly-situated cases' requires more than citing a few examples; one must distinguish those decisions from the present case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing other IPRs in which discretionary denial was not applied is insufficient unless the petitioner explains how those cases are factually similar and why they control. Blanket assertions of settled expectations or selective citations do not demonstrate abuse of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may order supplemental briefing to clarify application of precedent or new frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: In circumstances where clarification is needed about how Board precedent or a new discretionary framework applies, the Director may order additional briefing (see Ecto World and Apple v. Fintiv examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedential Director decisions (e.g., Ecto World, Fintiv) show the Director can require supplemental briefing when the Board’s application of precedent or a new discretionary approach is unclear. Parties seeking Director Review should be prepared to address how precedent and discretionary frameworks apply to their facts if supplemental briefing is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim processes for workload management can inform discretionary decisions (refer-or-deny option)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interim Processes for PTAB Workload Management explain that settled expectations (among other considerations) may support denying institution or referring a petition to the Board as part of workload management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process Memo functions as an interim framework for how the Office may manage PTAB workload; practitioners should understand it lists multiple discretionary considerations and contemplates referral to the Board as an alternative to institution or denial.
